items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: as a matter of fact we played around, we did quite a bit of recording, with different groups.

ctx.x: But things move on, you know, we progress. So I think it's very shortsighted on his part to, you know. But anyway, I got a chance to see Kenny Clark, again, on this trip because I remember -- I've known Kenny for years when he -- I think he was playing with Edgar Hayes when I first met Kenny somewhere. I was in Cincinnati with Roy Eldridge, playing the Cotton Club, and this is where I first met Kenny.
And then when I went to New York we became very good friends, as a matter of fact we played around, we did quite a bit of recording, with different groups. As a matter of fact I

think Kenny did some recording with Mildred Bailey too, during this time. But when I went to Europe I saw Kenny again. This is another time he'd left the -- I think this time he stayed though. No, he didn't either, he came back once again to the states to live. But at that time it was one -- in '47 he had left for good, you know. He got disgusted with America and the Jewish bebop as he called it, and went to Europe. But -- so I did some recording with Kenny over there, and I -- all I know it was for Nicole…
